𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟲 𝗵𝗮𝘀 𝗯𝗲𝗲𝗻 𝗮 𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗱 𝘆𝗲𝗮𝗿 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗰𝗮𝗽𝗶𝘁𝗮𝗹 𝗶𝗻 𝗜𝗻𝗱𝗼𝗻𝗲𝘀𝗶𝗮. The stock market is down around 𝟯𝟬%, the worst among major markets. MSCI is weighing a downgrade over governance and transparency. The rupiah crossed 𝟭𝟴,𝟬𝟬𝟬 to the dollar, and billions in portfolio money have left the country.

𝗔𝗻𝗱 𝘆𝗲𝘁 𝗱𝗶𝗿𝗲𝗰𝘁 𝗶𝗻𝘃𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗸𝗲𝗽𝘁 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗶𝗻𝗴. 𝗨𝗦𝗗 𝟱𝟳 𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗼𝗻 was realised in the first half, half of it foreign, and FDI grew 𝟮𝟳% year on year in the third quarter.
Portfolio money reacts to headlines. This year even gold, the classic safe haven, fell more than 𝟮𝟬% from its January record in a matter of days. Direct investment, the kind that builds hotels, factories and jobs, looks twenty years ahead. The real question is where it goes, and what it builds.

Tourism already generates 𝟰.𝟴% 𝗼𝗳 𝗜𝗻𝗱𝗼𝗻𝗲𝘀𝗶𝗮'𝘀 𝗚𝗗𝗣. That's more than palm oil (around 3.5%) and about twice real estate (around 2.4%). Only mining, oil and gas included, is clearly bigger, at 8.8%, and it shrank last year. Yet tourism receives 𝗹𝗲𝘀𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝗻 𝟰% 𝗼𝗳 𝗻𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝗮𝗹 𝗶𝗻𝘃𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁, and around three quarters of that still lands in Jakarta and Bali. The government's target is for tourism to reach 𝟴% 𝗼𝗳 𝗚𝗗𝗣 𝗯𝘆 𝟮𝟬𝟰𝟱.

The next markets are already visible: Lombok and Mandalika, Labuan Bajo, Lake Toba, Likupang. Visits to 𝗟𝗼𝗺𝗯𝗼𝗸 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗚𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘀 𝗿𝗲𝗰𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗹𝘆 𝗴𝗿𝗲𝘄 𝟳𝟮%. These destinations are poised to outgrow the national median, if access, infrastructure and the national masterplan deliver together.

One caution: tourism investment grew 𝟭𝟲.𝟲% in the first half, while international arrivals grew only 𝟱.𝟳%. Capital is arriving 𝘁𝗵𝗿𝗲𝗲 𝘁𝗶𝗺𝗲𝘀 𝗳𝗮𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗿 than foreign visitors. Underwrite accordingly, and price the currency: revenue comes in rupiah, even when expectations are set in dollars.
This is a market for 𝗽𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗲𝗻𝘁, 𝘄𝗲𝗹𝗹-𝘀𝘁𝗿𝘂𝗰𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲𝗱 𝗰𝗮𝗽𝗶𝘁𝗮𝗹. Fifteen years in investment management have taught me to ask six questions before any commitment:

→ 𝗪𝗵𝗲𝗿𝗲 exactly to deploy?
→ 𝗪𝗵𝗶𝗰𝗵 𝗮𝘀𝘀𝗲𝘁 𝗰𝗹𝗮𝘀𝘀, 𝘀𝗲𝗴𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝗶𝗻𝗴?
→ 𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗳𝗶𝗴𝘂𝗿𝗲𝘀 are really being underwritten?
→ What is the 𝗿𝗶𝘀𝗸-𝗮𝗱𝗷𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝗿𝗲𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗻, not just the headline IRR?
→ How will it be 𝗳𝗶𝗻𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲𝗱?
→ Who 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗼𝗹𝘀 it, and how do you 𝗲𝘅𝗶𝘁?

In Indonesia, most of those answers must be decided before the day the company is incorporated.

Part One of my analysis for My Lombok Magazine is in the comments.

MOBAVENUE AI TECH Ltd. (MOBAVENUE)

Mobavenue helps brands run digital advertising campaigns across 13 countries. It's not just a company that just displays ads ; it tries to find people who are more likely to download an app, make a purchase, or sign up.

Q2 FY27: Revenue grew 41.3% YoY to ₹76.7 Cr. EBITDA came in at ₹16.2 Cr (21.1% margin) and PAT at ₹11.3 Cr, up 54.8%. For H1FY27 revenue increased by 48.6% to ₹149.6 Cr, while PAT grew by 72.2% to ₹22.9 Cr.

1. Business Model : To a normal advertisement company, brands pays them to display their ads, even if nobody clicks or buys their products however the in case of Mobavenue, it earns money only when an actual user ends up becoming an an actual consumer. It does not own billboards, TV channels or other physical advertising assets. Most of its work happens through software and cloud servers.

2. Its AI Platform : Mobavenue has built its own system called the Neural Engine. It studies around 140 Cr user signals across 270 Cr devices every day and decides which ad to show,in less than 15 milliseconds. The idea is simple: show the right advertisement to someone who is more likely to respond.

3. International Business & RPO : International revenue has nearly doubled as a share of total revenue. It went from 12.3% to 23.8%. Across 13 countries the company now works with around 170 brands. Revenue Per Outcome (RPO) grew over 10% i.e. ₹50.67.
India brings more volume but at cheaper rates. To improve this, the company is now focusing  more on OTT, connected TVs, digital billboards and Apple devices. Countries like Indonesia and Philippines pay better RPO, while the US and UK generate higher RPO but have lower volumes.

4. Guidance & Customer Mix : Management expects to beat it's 30% full-year growth target. Management gave 2 reasons why its possible : (i) the festive season in India and (ii) year-end shopping in overseas markets. These should help in H2. Revenue Split : 65% from brands and 35% through agencies. Management expects this mix to remain similar for now but wants to add more direct clients over time.

5. PiX : Apple users are an important audience for advertisers because they generally spend more. Mobavenue launched PiX five months ago, building on Apple Search Ads to help brands advertise on iPhones, iPads and Apple TV. For now, the focus is on getting advertisers onto the platform, with new client additions expected by year-end. Revenue should follow as the business develops. A self-service version is also being developed for smaller app developers in countries such as Vietnam, Poland and the Netherlands, allowing them to run campaigns themselves.

Not investment advice.

🔹 Standards & Compliance: ASHRAE, ISO 16890, ISO 14644, WHO Guidelines, and applicable Indonesian regulations.

🔹 Air Filtration: Proper selection of pre-filters, fine filters, and HEPA filters based on actual requirements.

🔹 Indoor Air Quality: PM2.5, PM10, CO₂, VOC, temperature, and relative humidity.

🔹 Contamination Control: Dust, biological contaminants, and corrosive gases, especially in data centers.

🔹 Testing & Commissioning: Verification of airflow, ventilation rates, pressure relationships, filtration performance, and continuous monitoring.

I believe we need to move beyond simply installing air filters. We need an integrated approach covering Source Control, Ventilation, Filtration, Moisture Control, and Verification.

Searah Muara Bakau - Mooring Master (FPSO)
Apply before 04 Dec 2026

Job Description
Searah is a leading independent integrated energy company in Southeast Asia, established in 2026 through the strategic partnership between Eni and PETRONAS. With a current asset base of 19 assets across Malaysia and Indonesia, Searah stands as one of the leading players in the Asia Pacific energy sector. In Indonesia, Searah Muara Bakau serves as one of Searah’s operating companies. Its operations span the exploration, development, and production of offshore natural gas resources, with a strong focus on the deepwater areas of the Kutei Basin in the Makassar Strait, contributing to energy security across Southeast Asia and the sustainable development of the communities where it operates. We are looking for qualified personnel with high motivation, initiative, and integrity to fill the following position:

Job Title: Mooring Master

Purpose:
To act as a highly specialized and senior deck officer and responsible for the safe and efficient mooring, connecting, offloading, and unmooring of shuttle tankers (or offtake tankers) alongside the FPSO. The role demands ship handling knowledge, expert knowledge of dynamic positioning (DP) systems, and a comprehensive understanding of all associated marine operations, with strict adherence to Indonesian national regulations and international safety standards.

General Accountabilities and Responsibilities:
Primary Operational Duties: 
Offtake Tanker Operations: Act as the Person in Overall Advisory Control (POAC) for all offloading operations to shuttle tankers.
Pilotage & Ship Handling: Provide expert advice and direct the approach, positioning, and connection of the offtake tanker to the FPSO's stern or bow mooring system (STL - Single Point Mooring or Tandem Offloading).
Mooring & Connection: Supervise and ensure the safe connection of the offloading hawser or floating cargo hoses (for oil/condensate), including rigorous testing of the emergency release system (ERS).
Cargo Transfer: Supervise the entire cargo transfer process, including ballasting/deballasting coordination, constant monitoring of vessel positions, weather conditions, and hose integrity.
Unmooring: Direct the safe disconnection and unmooring of the tanker upon completion of offloading.
Emergency Response: Take immediate and decisive command in the event of an emergency during offloading operations (e.g., sudden bad weather, hose failure, tanker drive-off or drift-off). Execute emergency disconnect procedures (EDS) if necessary.

Planning & Communication: 
Briefings: Conduct pre-operation briefings (Pre-Transfer Conference) with the FPSO crew and the shuttle tanker's crew, covering all procedures, emergency plans, and communication protocols. 
Liaison: Serve as the primary marine liaison between the FPSO and the approaching/offtake tanker, as well as with FPSO Radio Operator and/or onshore traffic control (VTS - Vessel Traffic Service) if applicable.
Weather Monitoring: Continuously monitor and interpret weather forecasts and sea state conditions. Advise the OIM and Marine & Logistic Superintendent on the operational window and initiate delays or shutdowns if limits are exceeded.

Compliance & Administration (Critical for Indonesia): 
Ensure full compliance with all laws, decrees, and regulations issued by Indonesian authorities, including but not limited to: 
DIRJEN HUBLA (Directorate General of Sea Transportation): Monitor and comply with all maritime and shipping regulations. 
SKK Migas (Special Task Force for Upstream Oil and Gas Business Activities): Complete specific requirements for oil and gas operations. 
Indonesian Port Authority & Harbourmaster: Complete requirements for the specific offshore field location.
Documentation: Ensure all marine operations logs, offloading records, tanker paperwork (including validity of certifications and insurance), and pre-/post-operation checklists are accurately completed and filed. 
Permits & Clearances: Work with the company's marine department to ensure the offtake tanker has all necessary clearances and permits to operate in Indonesian waters.

Safety & Maintenance: 
Safety Leadership: Act as a Champion safety on deck during all offloading operations. Enforce the Permit to Work (PTW) system, isolation procedures, and stop-work authority.
System Checks: Oversee regular inspection and testing of all offloading equipment, including mooring hawsers, quick release hooks, hoses, and ESD/ERS systems.
Drills: Participate in and lead relevant emergency drills (e.g., oil spill response, emergency disconnect, man overboard).

Health, Safety, Environment and Quality (HSEQ): 
Comply with rules and standards described in Company Policies, HSE Integrated Management System and Procedures 
Report all incidents 
Motivate staff and colleagues to comply with HSE rules and standards 
Participate in HSE related initiatives
Requirements
Qualifications & Experience 
Education: Minimum Class-II Deck Officer (Ahli Nautika Tingkat II)
Professional Qualification: 
Minimum of 10 years of sea-going experience as a Master on large crude oil tankers (VLCC/ULCC) or LNG carriers is highly desirable.
Minimum 2 years’ experience of holding Maritime Pilot Class 1 for piloting unlimited vessel size  
Minimum 2 years’ experience as an Assistant Mooring Master. 
Successful completion of mooring/un-mooring operations proved by field competency assessment conducted by two qualified Mooring Master. 
Extensive and proven experience as a Mooring Master on an FPSO or an Aframax/Larger tanker is essential. Experience specifically in Southeast Asian waters is a significant advantage. 
Demonstrable experience in tandem offloading operations in dynamic positioning (DP) mode. 
Proven track record of handling emergency situations.
Certification, training and courses:
Valid STCW Certificates: Including Advanced Firefighting, Proficiency in Survival Craft, Medical First Aid, etc. 
DP Operator Certificate (Unlimited):  is highly desireable. 
Tanker Endorsements: Valid STCW certificates for Oil Tanker. 
Seafarer's Medical Certificate (valid).
Indonesian-specific Certifications: 
ADPT (Ahli Deklarasi Pengangkutan Tujuan) certification for hazardous cargo declaration. 
Local Indonesian Pilotage License/Certification may be required or highly advantageous.
Language: Proficient in English and Bahasa Indonesia 

Required Competencies 
Technical Competencies 
Expert Ship Handling: Deep understanding of vessel hydrodynamics, interaction, and forces involved in close-quarters maneuverings.

Non-Technical Competencies 
Leadership & Decision-Making: Ability to command respect, lead multi-national teams, and make critical decisions under extreme pressure.
Communication: Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English. Proficiency in Bahasa Indonesia is a HUGE advantage and is often a key differentiator for candidates, as it drastically improves coordination with local authorities and support vessels.
Problem-Solving: Strong analytical skills to quickly assess changing situations and implement solutions.
Safety Conscious: An unwavering commitment to a "Safety First" culture.
